set.body:
Build the reusable mathematical, concurrency, fuzz, allocation, and compatibility court that certifies the semantic kernel.

Reusable law modules
- Geometry: affine identity/inverse/composition; embedding/projection residual; point/vector laws; frame/grid alignment identity, reverse, composition, and transport.
- Axis: extent/coordinate laws, selection/permutation, record round trips.
- Sample space: logical shape, alignment, rebind, label independence, unit/convention participation.
- Sampled: map, exact-view, crop/flip/permutation/stride, copy/layout, rebind, aligned zip.
- Sampling: integer-coordinate exactness, constant/affine reproduction, validity bounds, frame rebind invariance.
- locus: ordinal conversion, deterministic keys, view/map commutation, region cardinality, packed order.
- NIfTI: endian/dtype/scaling, label exactness, qform/sform policy, extension alignment, random legal dimensions, malformed input, allocation bounds.

Infrastructure
- Property generators shrink to useful minimal failures.
- Malformed NIfTI fuzz/property jobs archive seeds and minimal reproductions.
- Registry concurrency tests run with parallel test execution enabled for the focused suites.
- CI covers at least JDK 17 and 21, JVM and Scala.js, optimized Scala.js links, and Node NIfTI tests.
- Add binary compatibility and semantic-version policy appropriate to the first public baseline.
- Large-allocation courts run in an isolated job with explicit host/source fingerprints.

Acceptance criteria
- ImageLaws is no longer limited to shape agreement and scalar approximate equality.
- Every new public algebraic operation has reusable laws and concrete regression tests.
- Test totals are not used as a substitute for semantic coverage.
- Fuzz, concurrency, allocation, and compatibility failures produce durable actionable artifacts.
- All implementation children are source-pinned and green before this issue closes.
set.title: Build the reusable semantic law, fuzz, concurrency, and CI court
